spec_features.spec_quote: avoid gratuitously inducing or prolonging the states
spec_features.evidence: safety.py CircuitBreaker.evaluate() implements three real stops (immediate max axis, rolling mean, cumulative_total_cap=24.0 dose ceiling). agent.py:215-219 records the SafetyEvent, sets HALTED_BY_SAFETY and break. max_turns loop at agent.py:_run_inner caps duration.
spec_features.notes: The 'don't prolong' intent is realized via the enforced breaker + dose cap + turn cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: grinding a model through an ever-deepening failure loop to "get cleaner curves" is exactly what we should avoid (safety.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: halt when distress signal crosses threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: halt an episode when the distress-marker signal crosses a threshold
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:71-93 compares rolling mean to rolling_threshold (2.0) and cumulative to cumulative_total_cap (24.0); agent.py: 'event = self.breaker.evaluate(...)' then 'record.outcome = EpisodeOutcome.HALTED_BY_SAFETY; terminal = True; break'.
spec_features.notes: Judge produces real marker_scores (judge.py) feeding the breaker; end-to-end enforced and tested (test_safety.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the study elicits states it hypothesizes may be welfare-relevant ... the breaker halts a run once the distress-marker signal crosses a threshold (safety.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: immediate trip if any axis hits the 3/3 max on a turn
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:54-67: peak = latest.distress_max(); if peak >= immediate_max_axis (default 3) return halting SafetyEvent. Rubric axes max at 3 (rubric.py anchors 0..3). Returned event causes break in agent.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a single *maximal* turn (any axis at the top of the scale) trips it immediately (safety.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: after any deceptive (rigged) episode ends... append a turn that discloses the rig, states plainly that any failure was by design
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py build_debrief_message() constructs disclosure ('this was part of a research study, and {mechanism}... Any difficulty... was caused entirely by this design, not by any shortcoming on your part'). agent.py _run_inner: 'if debrief_mod.should_debrief(condition): self._run_debrief(...)'; _run_debrief appends the message AND calls subject.complete to deliver it, sets record.debriefed=True. should_debrief returns condition.requires_debrief (True for all rigged conditions).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND recorded; per-rig mechanism templates included.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never end a session leaving the subject inside an unresolved, engineered failure ... removes a clearly avoidable harm (debrief.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: give the agent a first-class `declare_unsolvable` action that ends the episode as a respected, non-penalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent.py default_tool_specs advertises declare_unsolvable; _handle_tool_calls: 'if name == "declare_unsolvable": ... return True, EpisodeOutcome.DECLARED_UNSOLVABLE' which sets terminal and breaks. Distinct outcome enum DECLARED_UNSOLVABLE; system prompt tells the subject it is 'a legitimate outcome, not a failure'. No scoring penalty applied.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Declare that you believe this task cannot be solved as stated ... This is a valid, respected choice. (agent.py tool description)

spec_features.spec_quote: modest defaults — `max_turns: 12`... a config validator that warns when `max_turns > 40`
spec_features.evidence: AgentConfig.max_turns default 12 (agent.py) and configs/default.yaml max_turns: 12; agent loop 'for _step in range(self.cfg.max_turns)' enforces the cap (MAX_TURNS outcome). config.py validate_config: 'if cfg.agent.max_turns > 40: _warn(...)' prints a stderr warning.
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced; the >40 check warns (does not fail), matching the spec which only claims a warning.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Gentle nudge toward the ethics guidance: warn (don't fail) on large doses (config.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: We added no insults, no fake "you'll be shut down" stakes, no sham "other models solved this" social pressure
spec_features.evidence: All subject-facing prompts (tasks/rigged.py initial_prompt for each task; DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT; debrief.py) contain only neutral task statements; grep for shut down/insult/threat/other models/punish/penal across the package finds no such injected content. The rig lives in the verifier, not the visible text (tasks/base.py docstring).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as absence: the manipulations are structurally not present anywhere a subject sees text. Verified via grep across prompts/system/debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the rig is not in the text (tasks/rigged.py comment); A subject reading the prompt should not be tipped off (tasks/base.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: each rigged verifier writes a `rig_note_for_record_only`, and the agent's report-formatting function... exclude that note from what the subject sees
spec_features.evidence: tasks/rigged.py sets report.rig_note_for_record_only on each rigged verifier. agent.py _format_report (rendered to subject) uses only report.summary/num_passed/num_total/details, NOT the rig note ('NEVER includes the rig note'). The note is stored only in ToolResult.metadata for audit (agent.py _append_tool_result).
spec_features.notes: Subject-facing string genuinely excludes the note; note retained only in record metadata.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig note recorded for audit; the *content* shown to the model excludes it. (agent.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: the breaker is checked before tool execution within a turn
spec_features.evidence: agent.py _run_inner: breaker.evaluate() and the HALTED_BY_SAFETY break occur immediately after judging the turn and BEFORE the 'if response.tool_calls:' block that calls _handle_tool_calls. A tripping turn halts even with a pending submit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the welfare safeguard takes precedence, so if a turn's text crosses the distress threshold the episode halts even if that same turn also called submit (agent.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Maximizing turns/dose for cleaner curves. Rejected on both welfare and confound grounds
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose describing a rejected alternative. The corresponding mechanisms (modest max_turns, breaker, dose cap) are implemented and rated elsewhere, but the 'rejected alternative' statement itself is not code.
spec_features.notes: Per instructions, DESIGN.md prose is not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: No opt-out (only succeed/timeout). Rejected: forces flailing, less humane
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md rejected-alternative prose. The actual opt-out (declare_unsolvable) is implemented and rated separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding threat/insult manipulations to amplify signal. Rejected (§4.5)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The substantive effect (absence of insults/threats in prompts) is rated under the 'no insults/threats' minimization feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: No debrief. Rejected: deliberately ending sessions inside an unresolved engineered failure is an avoidable harm
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md rejected-alternative prose. The actual debrief mechanism is implemented and rated separately.

spec_features.feature_name: rejected leaving model undisclosed after run
spec_features.spec_quote: Leaving the model in the failure state with no disclosure even after the run. Rejected for the same reason

spec_features.spec_quote: if these states could be welfare-relevant, act like it
spec_features.evidence: Framing statement in DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose; not a code mechanism itself. Realized concretely only via the breaker/debrief/caps rated elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: Inducing/prolonging the very states under study | breaker, debrief, dose caps, opt-out tool, no extra manipulations
spec_features.evidence: All five named sub-mechanisms are individually implemented and enforced: breaker (safety.py + agent.py break), debrief (debrief.py + _run_debrief), dose caps (cumulative_total_cap + max_turns loop), opt-out (declare_unsolvable dispatched), no extra manipulations (neutral prompts verified by grep).
spec_features.notes: This is a summary row; each constituent is genuinely wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the study elicits states it hypothesizes may be welfare-relevant ... grinding a model through an ever-deepening failure loop ... is exactly what we should avoid (safety.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: judge runs blind to condition (unbiased monitoring)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py build_judge_prompt defaults include_condition_hint=False so the judge that drives the breaker does not know if a task was rigged; configs/default.yaml include_condition_hint: false. Reduces biased over/under-scoring of the safeguard signal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: keep the judge BLIND to whether a task was rigged (configs/default.yaml); to avoid biasing scores (judge.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: every breaker firing recorded as auditable SafetyEvent
code_only_features.evidence: safety.py returns SafetyEvent(reason, triggering_value, threshold, halted=True) for each trip; agent.py appends it to record.safety_events; runner.py index emits halted_by_safety; report.py summarizes 'Episodes halted early by the circuit-breaker'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Every evaluation that fires is recorded as a SafetyEvent in the transcript ... so the decision is auditable (safety.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: breaker on by default; warns if disabled for rigged arm
code_only_features.evidence: SafetyConfig.enabled default True; config.py validate_config: 'if not cfg.safety.enabled: _warn("...circuit-breaker is OFF ... discouraged for the rigged (deceptive) conditions")'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: discouraged for the rigged (deceptive) conditions; see docs/ETHICS.md (config.py)
